clinical_knowledge.topic: Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria evaluation and management
core_concepts: Chronic spontaneous urticaria is defined as recurrent hives (with or without angioedema) occurring almost daily for six weeks or more without an identifiable external trigger.
Individual wheals are transient, typically resolving within 24 hours, but new lesions continually appear elsewhere on the body.
Unlike acute urticaria, an external allergic trigger is rarely found; broad food or environmental allergy testing is usually unnecessary.
First-line treatment is scheduled (not as-needed) second-generation H1-antihistamines, up-titrated to up to four times the standard dose before considering omalizumab.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent itchy red welts on skin lasting less than 24 hours for 2 months

Key HPI features: 23F reports 2 months of daily, intensely itchy, raised red skin plaques (hives) that appear suddenly on various body parts. Each individual welt fades completely within 12-18 hours, but new ones appear constantly. No throat swelling.
Objective/Exam findings: Transient, blanching, erythematous wheals may be seen if examined during an active flare; none present between episodes. No angioedema.
common_misconceptions: Ordering extensive food or environmental allergy panels, which are rarely helpful since chronic spontaneous urticaria is not usually triggered by a specific allergen.
Treating antihistamines only as needed (PRN) rather than on a scheduled basis, which under-treats the daily symptom burden.
Assuming the condition is dangerous or airway-threatening when there is no angioedema or throat involvement.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to allergic contact dermatitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Individual welts lasting more than 24 hours or bruising.
management_principles: Explain that a specific external trigger is rarely identified in chronic spontaneous urticaria, unlike acute urticaria.
Start a scheduled (not PRN) second-generation antihistamine (e.g., fexofenadine or cetirizine), up-titrating to up to 4x standard dose if needed.
Consider omalizumab for antihistamine-refractory disease after specialist evaluation.
Refer to Allergy/Immunology if symptoms persist despite an adequate antihistamine trial.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Itchy hives appearing almost daily for six weeks or more, each welt fading within 24 hours, usually without an identifiable trigger.
red_flags: Individual welts lasting more than 24 hours or bruising

must_ask.say: How many weeks has this been happening?
Does each welt go away within a day?
Has your throat ever swollen or felt tight?
Have you noticed anything that seems to bring on new hives — a food, detergent, stress?
Have you had any allergy testing done for this?

history.answer: I have these itchy red welts that keep breaking out all over my skin.
It started about two months ago. Raised red welts appear out of nowhere almost every day.
They pop up on my arms, legs, back, and stomach without any set pattern.
They look like raised red bumps or hives, swollen like big mosquito bites. There are no blisters or scabs.
The itching is terrible and keeps me scratching constantly. They do not sting, burn, or ache.
Each individual welt fades completely away within 12 to 18 hours without leaving a trace, but new ones keep appearing.
I have never experienced anything like this before this started two months ago.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, fatigue, or muscle aches.
No, I do not have any blisters, sores, or irritation in my mouth, eyes, or genital area.
No, my skin does not peel or hurt, and the spots do not leave any dark bruises or purple marks behind.
No, my lips, tongue, and throat have never swollen, and I have had no shortness of breath or dizziness.
No, I have not started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, or pain relievers recently.
I switched my laundry detergent thinking it might be the cause, but the hives continued. I have not eaten unusual foods or handled new plants.
No one else in my household or at work has a rash or any itching.
I have not been bitten by bugs, traveled anywhere, or noticed cold, heat, or sweating triggering them.
No, I have never had eczema, asthma, seasonal allergies, or food allergies.
No, my joints do not hurt or swell, and my nails look completely normal.
I tried applying hydrocortisone cream from the drugstore, but it did not help the itching or stop new bumps.
No, I have never had skin prick testing or allergy blood tests done before.
I wonder if I suddenly developed an allergy to something I eat or the detergent I use.
The constant itching every single day is so frustrating, and it is making it hard to sleep and work.
I really want to get allergy testing done today so I can find out what is causing this and avoid it.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions or health problems.
I have never had surgery and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, regular over-the-counter medicines, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I do not smoke cigarettes or use e-cigarettes.
I drink an occasional beer or glass of wine socially once or twice a month.
I work full-time as a supermarket cashier and share an apartment with a roommate.
No one in my family has chronic hives, autoimmune disorders, or severe allergies.
I have one steady male partner, we use condoms, and I have never had any genital sores.
My last period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Alert young woman in no acute distress, with normal speech and no facial or periorbital swelling.
No active wheals, erythema, scaling, or excoriations visible; no dermographism or residual pigmentation noted.
Conjunctivae are clear and pink without injection; sclerae are anicteric.
Oral mucosa is moist and intact without lesions; no swelling of the lips, tongue, or uvula.
No palpable cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal heart sounds; no murmurs or friction rubs.
No swelling, warmth, erythema, or tenderness in peripheral joints; full active range of motion.
